subtitle: When Dragon and Clan Became a Kingdom

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Kangla ramparts with mist and coiled serpent-dragon form above
panels.action: Nongda Lairen Pakhangba stands upon an earthen embankment at Kangla, half in regal human form, half suggesting a vast coiled serpent-dragon in the clouds behind him, as the Imphal valley stretches out in early dawn mist.

dialogue.text: In Kangla’s mist, a serpent-dragon king is remembered as the first Meitei ruler—yet the records that praise him were stitched together centuries later.

i18n.hi: कंगला की धुंध में एक सर्प‑ड्रैगन राजा को पहले मीतै शासक की तरह याद किया जाता है, पर उसकी तारीफ करने वाले लेख बहुत बाद में जोड़े गए थे।

panels.shot: wide aerial over present-day Kangla ruins shifting into imagined ancient landscape
panels.action: An overhead view of the present-day earthen walls and moats of Kangla dissolves into an imagined earlier age of dense greenery, river channels, and scattered thatched settlements in the Imphal valley.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists clear the earth at Kangla and find layers of old occupation, but no clear stone that says, ‘Here a king began in 33 CE.’

i18n.hi: पुरातत्ववेत्ता कंगला की मिट्टी साफ़ करते हैं, पुरानी बसावट की कई परतें मिलती हैं, पर कहीं कोई पत्थर नहीं जो कहे, ‘यहाँ राजा ३३ ईस्वी में शुरू हुआ।’

panels.shot: intimate close-up on worn palm-leaf manuscripts lit by oil lamp
panels.action: A pair of careful hands turns fragile palm-leaf folios by lamplight, the Meitei script etched in dark lines while a faint outline of a dragon-serpent is seen in a margin.

dialogue.text: Instead we have words on palm leaves: the Cheitharol Kumpaba, copied and repaired in the eighteenth century from memories of earlier chronicles now lost.

i18n.hi: इसके बदले हमारे पास ताड़पत्र पर लिखे शब्द हैं: चеитरोल कुम्पाबा, जिसे अठारहवीं सदी में पुराने, खोए इतिवृत्तों की याद से दोबारा नकल‑मरम्मत किया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of 18th-century royal scribes in a wooden hall
panels.action: Inside a wooden hall, royal scribes sit cross-legged, listening to elder reciters as they scratch lines onto new palm leaves, a faint image of a royal courtyard taking shape in their imagination.

dialogue.text: Those scribes remembered and argued, piecing together lists of kings and events, sewing oral tales into the royal diary of Manipur.

i18n.hi: उन लिपिकारों ने यादें जोड़ीं, बहसें कीं, राजाओं और घटनाओं की सूचियाँ सिलीं, लोककथाओं को मिलाकर मणिपुर की राज‑दैनिकी बना दी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the name of Nongda Lairen Pakhangba in manuscript
panels.action: The camera closes in on a line in the manuscript where the name ‘Nongda Lairen Pakhangba’ stands out, framed by decorative flourishes resembling serpent coils.

dialogue.text: Near the beginning of that reconstructed scroll, one name glows: Nongda Lairen Pakhangba, given an accession in the year we call 33 CE.

i18n.hi: उस दोबारा गढ़ी शुरुआत के पास एक नाम चमकता है: नोंग्दा लैरेन पाखंगबा, जिसे हमारे हिसाब से ३३ ईस्वी में गद्दी मिली।

panels.shot: mythic wide shot of human figure merging with serpent-dragon over riverbank
panels.action: By a winding river under stormy clouds, Nongda Lairen Pakhangba stands at the water’s edge as a gigantic serpent-dragon rises behind him, their silhouettes overlapping like two faces of one being.

dialogue.text: In older Meitei ritual texts, Pakhangba is not only a man. He is a dragon-serpent deity, coiling under earth and sky, guarding clans and kings.

i18n.hi: पुरानी मीतै पूजा‑पुस्तकों में पाखंगबा केवल आदमी नहीं, वह सर्प‑ड्रैगन देवता है, धरती‑आसमान के नीचे कुंडली मारे, कुलों और राजाओं की रखवाली करता है।

panels.shot: panoramic wide of seven clustered settlements around Kangla marshes
panels.action: A wide view shows seven clusters of thatched houses around wetlands and raised mounds, each with its own small shrine and gathering fire, separated by fields and streams.

dialogue.text: Tradition speaks of seven clans in the valley, each with its own hearth, deity and leader, often wary of one another yet sharing the same rivers and rains.

i18n.hi: परंपरा घाटी के सात कुलों की बात करती है, हर एक का अपना चूल्हा, देवता और मुखिया, आपस में सजग, पर एक ही नदियाँ और बारिश बाँटते।

panels.shot: medium shot of clan leaders in council ring under open sky
panels.action: In an open clearing near Kangla, several clan chiefs sit in a circle on woven mats, while Nongda Lairen Pakhangba stands at the edge, calm and attentive, his eyes moving from face to face.

dialogue.text: The Puya traditions tell of councils, of clan heads debating under open sky, and of Pakhangba emerging as the one who could bind them without breaking them.

i18n.hi: पुया परंपराएँ सभाओं की कहती हैं, खुले आसमान के नीचे कुल प्रमुखों की बहसें, और पाखंगबा का उभरना उस शख्स के रूप में जो सबको जोड़े, किसी को तोड़े बिना।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Pakhangba swearing oath at Kangla mound
panels.action: On a raised earth mound at Kangla, Pakhangba stands before a simple wooden post wrapped with cloth, touching it with both hands as clan elders watch in tense silence.

dialogue.text: The Cheitharol Kumpaba says he was enthroned at Kangla, the central mound becoming more than a village—it became the remembered heart of a kingdom.

i18n.hi: चеитरोल कुम्पाबा कहता है, उसे कंगला में बैठाया गया, बीच की वह टीली गाँव से बढ़कर बनी—यादों में पूरे राज्य का दिल।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of the Kuchu court in session
panels.action: Inside a thatched hall, Pakhangba sits on a low wooden platform as men and women stand before him in orderly rows, while officials to one side whisper and take mental note.

dialogue.text: Later memory names his court the Kuchu, where disputes were heard and judgments given, not just by force of spear but by shared hearing.

i18n.hi: बाद की यादें उसके दरबार को ‘कुचु’ कहती हैं, जहाँ झगड़े सुने जाते थे, फैसले दिए जाते थे, केवल भाले से नहीं, साझा सुनवाई से।

panels.shot: wide shot of ritual specialists gathered in a semi-circle
panels.action: A semi-circle of ritual specialists, some with drums, others with feathered staffs, stand before Pakhangba in the courtyard, as smoke from incense pots curls up into the morning air.

dialogue.text: Religious councils like the Patcha Loishang enter the story here, weaving deities and rites into the fabric of rule, though scholars remind us these details come from much later pens.

i18n.hi: पचा लोईशंग जैसे धार्मिक परिषद यहीं कहानी में घुसते हैं, देवताओं और अनुष्ठानों को राजकाज की बुनावट में बुनते हुए, हालांकि विद्वान याद दिलाते हैं कि ये बातें भी बहुत बाद की कलमों से आईं।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of men training with spears near riverbank
panels.action: By a riverside clearing, groups of young men train with long spears and shields under the watchful gaze of Pakhangba, who stands with arms folded, measuring their discipline.

dialogue.text: Stories of early lallup—rotating service for labour and war—are pushed back onto his reign, sketching an image of a community learning to move as one body.

i18n.hi: शुरुआती लल्लुप की कहानियाँ—घूम‑घूम कर श्रम और युद्ध सेवा—भी उसके राज पर डाल दी जाती हैं, जैसे कोई समुदाय पहली बार एक शरीर की तरह चलना सीख रहा हो।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Pakhangba’s face half-lit, contemplative at night
panels.action: At night, Pakhangba sits alone on the Kangla mound, his face half in lamplight, half in shadow, as distant torches mark the clan settlements around.

dialogue.speaker: nongda_lairen_pakhangba
dialogue.text: If I am dragon and man, whose hunger do I feed first—clan or kingdom?

i18n.hi: अगर मैं ड्रैगन भी हूँ और इंसान भी, पहले किसकी भूख भरूँ—कुल की या राज्य की?

panels.shot: mythic interior shot of ritual where Pakhangba’s human figure is encircled by serpent form
panels.action: Inside a dim shrine, Pakhangba stands rigid as dancers in serpent masks coil around him, their movement suggesting a giant unseen dragon looping his body.

dialogue.text: Ritual dramas, preserved far later, recall him as both king and coiling god—an image Rodney Sebastian sees as a fusion of polity and sacred power.

i18n.hi: बहुत बाद तक निभाई गई नाटकीय रीतें उसे राजा और कुंडली मारते देव दोनों की तरह दिखाती हैं—एक तस्वीर जिसे रॉडनी सेबास्टियन सत्ता और पवित्र शक्ति के मेल के रूप में देखते हैं।

panels.shot: cutaway to modern scholar at desk with books and field notes
panels.action: A modern scholar sits at a cluttered desk, open books on Meitei ritual and the Cheitharol Kumpaba spread out, while photographs from Kangla excavations are pinned behind them.

dialogue.text: Modern historians, like Parratt, step carefully here, reminding us that this early portion of the chronicle is a later reconstruction, not a diary kept in his own time.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार, जैसे पेरट, यहाँ क़दम सँभालकर रखते हैं, याद दिलाते हैं कि इतिवृत्त का यह शुरुआती हिस्सा बाद की जोड़‑घटत है, न कि उसके समय की रोज़‑रोज़ लिखी डायरी।

panels.shot: wide twilight shot of Kangla moats and walls in present, with faint overlay of ancient court
panels.action: At twilight, the present-day moats and earthen embankments of Kangla are quiet, while a faint ghostly overlay suggests an earlier court scene playing upon the same ground.

dialogue.text: Post-2004 work at Kangla confirms long human presence, yet offers no clear throne of 33 CE, no inscribed stone naming Pakhangba there and then.

i18n.hi: २००४ के बाद का कंगला शोध लम्बी बस्ती दिखाता है, पर ३३ ईस्वी का कोई साफ़ तख़्त नहीं, कोई पत्थर नहीं जो वहीं‑उसी वक्त पाखंगबा का नाम खोदे।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of Pakhangba standing between clans, river and shrine
panels.action: In a symbolic composition, Pakhangba stands at the center, with stylized clan settlements to one side, a river and fields to another, and a serpent-shaped shrine behind him, all balanced in a fragile triangle.

dialogue.text: Even if we cannot map his every step, the remembered Pakhangba marks where Meitei storytellers chose to place the hinge between scattered clans and a named Kangleipak.

i18n.hi: भले हम उसका हर क़दम न नाप सकें, यादों वाला पाखंगबा दिखाता है कि मीतै कथाकारों ने बिखरे कुलों और नामदार कंगलेइपाक के बीच की कुंडी कहाँ लगाई।

panels.shot: close-up on young Meitei child listening to elder recounting story by fire
panels.action: By a household hearth, a child leans forward wide-eyed as an elder gestures with hands, tracing an invisible serpent in the air while others listen in quiet attention.

dialogue.text: Each retelling, in courtyards and chronicles, chose what to remember and what to forget, turning a possible early ruler into a dragon-king who holds clans and gods together.

i18n.hi: हर दोहराव—आँगनों में, इतिवृत्तों में—ने चुना क्या याद रखना है, क्या छोड़ना है, एक शायद‑सा शुरुआती शासक बदल गया ऐसे ड्रैगन‑राजा में जो कुलों और देवताओं को साथ बाँधता है।

panels.shot: final wide shot of Pakhangba fading into Kangla landscape at dawn
panels.action: As dawn light spills over the Kangla landscape, Pakhangba’s figure stands briefly and then fades into the mists, leaving only the earthworks, trees, and river glinting in the sun.

dialogue.text: Seen through both faith and doubt, Nongda Lairen Pakhangba reminds us that founding myths gain their power when we honour them as stories—and still ask where history begins.

i18n.hi: श्रद्धा और संदेह, दोनों की नज़र से देखो तो नोंग्दा लैरेन पाखंगबा याद दिलाता है कि संस्थापक कथाएँ तब ताक़त पाती हैं, जब हम उन्हें कहानी मानकर सम्मान दें—और फिर भी पूछें कि असली इतिहास कहाँ से शुरू होता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Dragon and Clan Became a Kingdom
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब ड्रैगन और कुल मिलकर बना एक राज्य
